## What is marketing automation software?

### Automation

Marketing automation tools are part of a larger marketing software platform. They let you set up automated sequences to do a series of tasks. Without automating, you’d be doing these tasks yourself, slowly, and one at a time. That’s what automation features do. They take over repetitive tasks to save human agents time and effort.

So how is this applied to marketing? It’s mostly based on email campaigns, but there’s plenty of social media ads and SMS marketing too. It all starts with workflows.

### Workflows

Let’s use an example to explain workflows: 

Firstly, think of posting an ad on Facebook to everyone who has liked your page. When someone clicks an ad, an automation workflow kicks in. It can send them an email with a link, and if they click that, it can show them custom items picked for them based on past online behavior. Or, for those who look at the ad but don’t open the email, another branch of the automation sequence may do something else, like send them a promotion email.

And it all happens without you having to do anything. You only get involved at key moments.

Good marketing automation platforms often have templates for workflows. These you can also edit using a visual dashboard. It generally looks like you're building a tree, where _If-Then_ logic makes the either-or branches. Drag and drop lets you easily block out these workflows. 

### Segmentation

Another useful tool is audience segmentation. You can automate so that all your contacts can be grouped under various tags. This is based on the data you have in their profiles or what the software can gather from their company and social sites. You can also edit the segments and create custom tags and groups. 

This enhances a marketing automation platform’s ability to customize content for each contact you’re reaching out to. For example, An online sports store mailing out an email newsletter to all their subscribers can have different background pictures based on the customer’s purchase history (eg: baseball for you, rock-climbing for me). It can also segment them based on demographics, which device they use, or geolocations.

### Predictive analytics

Marketing automation tools can also be used for [predictive functionality](https://crm.org/news/best-predictive-analytics-tools). It can look at all the activity in your campaign engagements or your funnels. Using data of your successes and drop offs, it can optimize all sorts of marketing decisions. These include finding the best time of day to post and ad or send an email. It also does lead scoring, telling you the likeliness of someone to engage or purchase.

In the end, you can say that marketing automation software is sort of like the lubricant connecting the marketing and sales pipelines. It both helps find new customers and nurture those customers down the funnel.

## What is the best marketing automation software? Here’s our top 20 list:

![best marketing automation software](https://crm.org/sites/default/files/imce/crm_org_hub_marketing_automation_software_cosmos_of_logos-02.svg)

Now that you’ve gone and learned about the features and functions of automation tools for marketing, it’s time to check out some of the best marketing automation software around today. We compare ones for big business and smaller businesses, and even find some free versions in the stack.

### 1\. ActiveCampaign (Best marketing automation software overall)

![ActiveCampaign best marketing automation software](https://crm.org/sites/default/files/imce/crm_org_hub_marketing_automation_software_activecampaign-01.svg)

ActiveCampaign bills itself as customer experience automation. This is one of the best platforms overall. It combines a CRM solution with email marketing in a marketing automation platform. ActiveCampaign has solutions for sales, marketing and customer support.

You get many good marketing automation tools. These include automated workflows which can become drip campaigns. Customers in your CRM can be tagged and labelled. This lets you target specific marketing messaging to their needs. There are form tools which turn interested people into leads.

ActiveCampaign lets you build a multi-channel marketing strategy. You get to apply marketing tools to social media too. As leads respond to marketing efforts, ActiveCampaign gets you lead scoring. 

ActiveCampaign has price buckets. The most affordable is $9 per month billed annually. But for more serious marketing automation you probably need the Plus plan at $49 per month billed annually.

ActiveCampaign is best for:

*   Individual users
*   Startups
*   SMBs
*   E-commerce
*   Customer relationship management
*   Marketing automation
*   Audience segment
